suspect_claims.claim: L49, L124, numbers table: Remento completion proxy of ≈16 stories per order (1,000,000 stories ÷ 64,000 orders) against 52 prompts.
suspect_claims.problem: Mismatched dates. The $7M statement aired 2026-03-25 (Shark Tank S17 E15, per Rotten Tomatoes / Military.com via search); the 1M+ story count is the Nov 2026 homepage. The file's own source S19 gives a contemporaneous count it ignores: "Remento recently celebrated recording more than 500,000 stories." Same-date ratio is ≈ 500,000 ÷ 64,000 ≈ 7.8, about half the published figure. The file uses the 16 as falsification evidence in Q8.

suspect_claims.claim: L33: Storyworth funding -- "No priced round located ... amount raised [unknown]".
suspect_claims.problem: One search contradicts the [unknown]. CB Insights financials page (fetched): "StoryWorth has raised $150K over 2 rounds ... latest funding round was a Seed for $0.15M on January 28, 2011", investors listed as Y Combinator and Felicis. It is an aggregator and needs an estimator label, but the brief asked for funding and the file reports none.

suspect_claims.claim: L36: "TV and Facebook spend: [unknown — searched, nothing located]".
suspect_claims.problem: TV as a channel is easily evidenced. iSpot.tv lists four Storyworth national TV spots ("Dad: Every Family" Jun 2021, "Adrianne" Apr 2022, "Dear Dad" Jun 2022, "Mother's Day: Dear Mom"). Tatari published "How Storyworth Used TV Ads for a Successful Holiday Season" (2023-09-29, fetched) with Head of Marketing Greg Kapp: "Lowered CPV (cost per visitor) and CPA (cost per acquisition)". Spend is unknown, but the channel and its Father's Day / Mother's Day / holiday timing are not.

suspect_claims.claim: L7, L29, comparables: Storyworth revenue "roughly $14M–$45M a year [estimated]".
suspect_claims.problem: Assumption stacked on assumption (15–25% of lifetime books in the last 12 months; 0.5–1.0 books per plan; $90 net), none evidenced, yet promoted to the Bottom line and the comparables table. The anchor "Over 1,000,000 books printed" is a floor that is probably stale: a search snippet shows the same "Over 1 million books printed since 2013" on an older Storyworth landing page headed "HOLIDAY SALE: $15 OFF THROUGH DEC 31" (a prior season; page now 404), and HNGN reported it in Apr 2026. Wayback was unreachable, so first-use date is unverified. Inconsistent rounding too: $14M in the Bottom line, $13.5M in the table.

suspect_claims.claim: L8: "more plans in one year than Storyworth has printed books in its whole life [sourced: S1]".
suspect_claims.problem: S1 says "Over 1,000,000 books printed", a floor. Comparing 1.1M to a floor of unknown true value is an inference, not a sourced fact; the tag overstates it.

suspect_claims.claim: L122, numbers table: storyworth.com "603.8K visits over three months and −22.46% month-on-month"; "Direct = 55.65% of desktop visits" (Similarweb, Aug 2026).
suspect_claims.problem: Estimator-only, snippet-only, suspiciously precise and not reproducible: similarweb.com returned HTTP 202 (bot wall) and a search for "603.8K" / "22.46%" found nothing. A Semrush snapshot found by the same search shows 405.69K–756.16K visits per month and 76.03% direct, so "over three months" is probably a misread monthly figure. This is the only traffic evidence behind the Q8 'not stalling' reading.

suspect_claims.claim: L7, L48, L148: largest sourced revenue = Remento ">$7 million in sales in under twelve months after its 2025 deal closed"; cumulative ≥ $7.62M.
suspect_claims.problem: The quote is real (S19, S20 fetched) but the file never dates the statement: the episode aired 2026-03-25, so the figure is at least 8 months old and says nothing about the 2026 run-rate. "2025 deal" is the file's assumption; the source gives no closing date. Primetimer's own subhead calls it "revenue" while the founder says "sales"; gross vs net is unknown and it is unaudited. The $7.62M sum adds two non-adjacent periods.

suspect_claims.claim: L30: Scenario B "≥ $11.5M–$20.8M" from stories rising 35M (Feb 2026) to 40M (Jul–Nov 2026).
suspect_claims.problem: Neither counter is dated by Storyworth. The 35M comes from a TechTimes piece; Wikipedia only says "as of 2026". If 35M was already old site copy, the growth rate is overstated. Stories ÷ 52 is also not a strict floor on paid plans, because storytellers keep writing after the paid year (S1 FAQ: "You'll have access to write ... even after your plan year has ended").

suspect_claims.claim: L37, L111, L31: S9 (HNGN, 2026-04-30) used as press for "holiday gifting drives much of the company's annual customer acquisition", "typically as a gift" and the 2014 $49 price.
suspect_claims.problem: The page footer reads "This is a contributed article. The HNGN news staff was not involved in the creation of this article." It is placed/PR content, not independent reporting. The 2014 price was also "$49 a year for six people", which the lifetime-floor arithmetic ignores.

suspect_claims.claim: L11, L102: AI voice cost "≈ $6–$22 per recipient-year, or 6–22% of a $99 price".
suspect_claims.problem: The upper bound drops the file's own Retell ceiling ($48.36 at $0.31/min, about 49% of $99 before telephony). ElevenLabs $0.08/min excludes LLM cost (S40: LLM "Based on usage and varies by model. At cost"). The range also excludes chapter-writing LLM cost, retries and unanswered calls, which the file notes but does not price.

suspect_claims.claim: L83: "None of the eight verified products runs an interviewer over the family's own photos".
